en.title: The present perfect
en.summary: The present perfect links the past with the present.

paragraphs: The present perfect describes a past action or state that is connected to the present: its result is visible now, it continues up to now, or it happened at an unstated time. It is formed with have or has and the past participle.

items: I **have lost** my keys. (I still cannot find them.)
She **has lived** here for ten years. (She still lives here.)
Have you **ever been** to Japan? (at any time in your life)

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementI have finished. She has finished.
questionHave you finished? Has she finished?
negativeI have not (haven't) finished. She hasn't finished.
short formI've, you've, she's, they've

paragraphs: The past participle of regular verbs ends in -ed, like the simple past. Irregular verbs have special participles: go → gone, see → seen, write → written, be → been.

blocks.html:
MeaningTime wordsExample
result nowjust, already, yetI have just seen him.
experienceever, never, beforeI have never been to Rome.
duration up to nowfor, sinceWe have lived here since 2018.
unfinished periodtoday, this week, this yearI have seen three films this week.

paragraphs: Use the simple past when the time is finished and stated (yesterday, in 2010, last week). Use the present perfect when the time is not stated or the period is not finished.

blocks.html:
Simple pastPresent perfect
I saw him yesterday.I have seen him today.
She lived in Paris in 2010.She has lived in Paris for ten years.
Did you ever go to Spain? (a specific time)Have you ever been to Spain?

items: Wrong: **I have seen him yesterday.** Right: **I saw him yesterday.**
Wrong: **I am living here since 2018.** Right: **I have lived here since 2018.**
Wrong: **She has went home.** Right: **She has gone home.**
